bundle.author: hhkarimi
bundle.title: [DATA-2626] Add Serve Priority Segment flag and HubSpot contact attribute feed
bundle.body:
## What changed

This PR adds a **Serve Priority Segment** flag for GTM outreach ([DATA-2626](https://app.clickup.com/t/17tnw2b3v4c)), plus a feed that writes it onto existing HubSpot contacts.

- `icp_normalized_position_names` gets a `serve_priority` column. It is true for legislative positions in the city, town, township and metro categories, and for `City Executive//Mayor` and `Township Mayor`. The seed is set to `full_refresh` so the new column applies itself in every environment.
- `int__icp_offices.is_serve_priority_segment` is true when the position has `serve_priority`, more than 5,000 voters, and is neither judicial nor appointed. It is empty when the voter count is unknown. It does not depend on Win ICP, so offices over 100K voters qualify.
- `int__hubspot_contacts` passes the flag through, using the contact's effective BallotReady position.
- `candidacy_hubspot` gets `serve_priority_segment`, so net-new leads arrive flagged. It is false when the position is unresolved, with no fallback to matching on office-name text.
- New `contact_attributes_hubspot` view: one row per existing HubSpot contact (`Record ID`) where our value differs from HubSpot's. It is the contact-level companion to `company_viability_hubspot`.
  - Our unknowns are not sent.
  - A HubSpot `true` we no longer support is set to `false`.
- `hubspot_contact_property_columns` registers the `serve_priority_segment` property, so staging reads HubSpot's value back for the diff.

## Why

GTM wants one Databricks-defined true/false property to prioritize outreach, instead of rebuilding the logic from several HubSpot fields. This is an outreach segment, not a change to the governed ICP definitions.

`candidacy_hubspot` only creates contacts, so on its own it would never flag contacts that already exist. The diff feed covers them. HubSpot has no values for the property yet, so its first run is the backfill.

## Verification (dev, `dbt build`)

- Seeds, `int__icp_offices`, the HubSpot staging model, `int__hubspot_contacts`, `candidacy_hubspot`, `contact_attributes_hubspot` and their tests: all pass. The one warning, `assert_candidacy_hubspot_candidate_code_collision` (3), comes from an existing test.

| | True | False | Empty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Positions | 19,037 | 266,977 | 2,070 |
| HubSpot contacts | 24,648 | 99,939 | 218,620 (no resolved position) |
| `contact_attributes_hubspot` rows | 24,648 | 99,939 | not sent |

- 1,411 of the flagged contacts are not Win ICP. These are offices over 100K voters, which is intended.
- Flagged contacts by position: City Legislature 18,628; Mayor 4,274; Township Trustee/Council 1,369; Council Chair 136; Township Mayor 83; other town and city legislative positions 155.

## Notes

- Positions included or left out by judgement: Town Moderator, Town Meeting Board, Board of Selectmen and Board of Finance are in (150 contacts, none with a Nov 3 election). Vice-Mayor/Mayor Pro Tem and City Manager/First Selectman are out. Changing any of them is one seed cell.
- A few city council districts show state-sized voter counts (up to 17.7M). The district matching behind those counts was already like this before this PR. They clear the 5K threshold either way.
- No semantic-layer change.

diff --git a/dbt/project/models/marts/sales_reverse_etl/contact_attributes_hubspot.sql b/dbt/project/models/marts/sales_reverse_etl/contact_attributes_hubspot.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..26719ce
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dbt/project/models/marts/sales_reverse_etl/contact_attributes_hubspot.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,47 @@
+{{ config(materialized="view", tblproperties={}) }}
+
+-- Databricks-owned attributes -> EXISTING HubSpot contacts, matched on Record ID.
+-- Contact-grained companion to company_viability_hubspot; candidacy_hubspot is the
+-- feed that creates contacts. New contact attributes we own belong here as columns.
+--
+-- A diff, not a snapshot: a row per contact where a published value differs from
+-- HubSpot's current (Airbyte-ingested) value. The first run after a property is
+-- created is therefore its backfill, and later runs carry only changes.
+--
+-- An unknown on our side (no resolved position, or an unsized district) is not
+-- sent, so it stays blank in HubSpot rather than being asserted false. Exception:
+-- a stale HubSpot true is cleared to false so it cannot keep a lead at the top of
+-- the outreach queue.
+--
+-- A view, like the company feed: ops reads it right before an import and wants
+-- current values, and both inputs are already materialized. Empty tblproperties:
+-- the schema's Delta column mapping is meaningless on a view.
+with
+    compared as (
+        select
+            ours.id,
+            case
+                when ours.is_serve_priority_segment is not null
+                then ours.is_serve_priority_segment
+                when theirs.serve_priority_segment
+                then false
+            end as serve_priority_segment,
+            theirs.serve_priority_segment as hs_serve_priority_segment
+        from {{ ref("int__hubspot_contacts") }} as ours
+        -- INNER join: a contact missing from the ingest no longer exists in
+        -- HubSpot and would only error on import.
+        join
+            {{ ref("stg_airbyte_source__hubspot_api_contacts") }} as theirs
+            on ours.id = theirs.id
+    )
+
+select
+    id as `Record ID`,
+    serve_priority_segment,
+    hs_serve_priority_segment as hubspot_current_serve_priority_segment
+from compared
+-- equal_null treats a blank HubSpot value as a difference, which is what makes
+-- the first run fill every contact we have a value for.
+where
+    serve_priority_segment is not null
+    and not equal_null(serve_priority_segment, hs_serve_priority_segment)

findings.body: When `icp_position_names.name is null` (the position exists in BallotReady but has no matching row in the seed), this CASE returns `false` rather than `null`. That `false` propagates unchanged through `int__hubspot_contacts` into `contact_attributes_hubspot`, where it passes the `WHERE serve_priority_segment IS NOT NULL` filter and is written to HubSpot. This contradicts the stated design in `contact_attributes_hubspot.sql` ("An unknown on our side … is not sent, so it stays blank in HubSpot rather than being asserted false") and the YAML description ("Null when the contact has no resolved position"). The fix is to return `null` when the position is unrecognized (name is null), while keeping `false` for positions that are known-ineligible (judicial, appointed, or `serve_priority = false`). Falsification check: no upstream conversion of `false` to `null` exists on the path from `int__icp_offices` → `int__hubspot_contacts` → `contact_attributes_hubspot`; the value passes through unchanged.
findings.suggestion:
case
    when position.is_judicial or position.is_appointed
    then false
    when icp_position_names.name is null
    then null
    when not icp_position_names.serve_priority
    then false
    when voter_count is null
    then null
    else voter_count > 5000
end as is_serve_priority_segment

output.summary: This PR adds a Serve Priority Segment flag across the dbt pipeline — from a new `serve_priority` column in the `icp_normalized_position_names` seed, through `int__icp_offices`, `int__hubspot_contacts`, `candidacy_hubspot` (for new contacts), and a new `contact_attributes_hubspot` diff-view (for existing contacts). The scout flagged five areas: (1) false-vs-null semantics for unmatched positions, (2) stale-true clearance logic in the contact feed, (3) mayor rows in the seed CSV, (4) the join key between `candidacy_scored` and `int__icp_offices`, and (5) the not_null test boundary on the contact feed. Deep review confirmed that the seed correctly flags mayors as `serve_priority=true`, the join key `br_position_database_id` exists in `candidacy_scored`, the stale-true clearance logic handles all nine (ours × theirs) combinations correctly, and the not_null test is tautological but harmless. One blocker was confirmed: unrecognized positions (no seed match) return `false` instead of `null`, causing the contact feed to assert "not in segment" for genuinely unknown contacts rather than leaving HubSpot blank, contradicting the model's own documented intent.

findings.body: When `icp_position_names.name is null` (the position exists in BallotReady but has no matching row in the seed), this CASE returns `false` rather than `null`. That `false` propagates unchanged through `int__hubspot_contacts` into `contact_attributes_hubspot`, where it passes the `WHERE serve_priority_segment IS NOT NULL` filter and is written to HubSpot. This contradicts the stated design in `contact_attributes_hubspot.sql` ("An unknown on our side … is not sent, so it stays blank in HubSpot rather than being asserted false") and the YAML description ("Null when the contact has no resolved position"). The fix is to return `null` when the position is unrecognized (name is null), while keeping `false` for positions that are known-ineligible (judicial, appointed, or `serve_priority = false`). Falsification check: no upstream conversion of `false` to `null` exists on the path from `int__icp_offices` → `int__hubspot_contacts` → `contact_attributes_hubspot`; the value passes through unchanged.
findings.suggestion:
case
    when position.is_judicial or position.is_appointed
    then false
    when icp_position_names.name is null
    then null
    when not icp_position_names.serve_priority
    then false
    when voter_count is null
    then null
    else voter_count > 5000
end as is_serve_priority_segment
